I am farming cassava and sweet potato here in Mwanza on my own land. The rains come once a year so I must plan carefully, but tubers like cassava are forgiving and do not need much fertilizer — I rely on the manure from my few goats and the ash from cooking. Chemical fertilizer is expensive and I would rather spend that money on my maize plot or school fees; for roots the local varieties my neighbors share have always grown well enough. I intercrop with beans or maize to get more from the same land, and most of the work — planting, weeding, harvesting — my wife and I handle ourselves, hiring a few people only for the heavy weeding when the rains come strong.
